w: At 1.00 p.m. Swamishri departed from Mumbai and arrived at Rajkot airport at 2.57 p.m. By the time Swamishri reached the mandir it was 3.35 p.m. More than 400 devotees had been waiting in the hot afternoon sun for Swamishri’s darshan. Though it was late Swamishri addressed the devotees saying,"... We are late. And when it’s late one thinks when will (Swami) come? Though one feels that one has missed some work at home because of the delay still one has got the opportunity of God’s darshan, the darshan of the mandir’s flag, kalash and all these sadhus and devotees assembled here. So the delay here (in the mandir) is for your good because it is for your moksha. Otherwise, for infinite births you have been late and delayed! Because as long as you had not met God and His holy sadhu, you were late..."
Swamishri arrived at Visavadar at 10.00 am. 3,500 devotees and well wishers were present during the murti pratishtha and assembly. After having lunch Swamishri returned to Junagadh at 1.50 p.m.

G od says to Naradji, "To my mind there is no one greater than the sant (holy sadhu)." But why is the sant the greatest? Because he communicates the true glory of God to man and inspires profound faith for Him. .

w: At 5.30 pm the 'Swayam Sevak Din' (Volunteers' Day) assembly commenced. Incidents on the tremendous sacrifice of volunteers were narrated. A drama presentation on 'Samat Patel's' sacrifice to please Lord Swaminarayan was made by the volunteers. Then volunteers representing the 34 departments behind the Haveli Mahotsav came to receive Swamishri's blessings. As each departmental representative came, a prayer was offered to Swamishri. Swamishri finally crowned the 'Swayam Sevak Din' with his blessings.
During the evening satsang assembly, Swamishri was honored with a citation presented by the officials of the city municipalty.
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for Lathidad hari mandir. Swamishri blessed the local devotees and showered rice grains on them.
In the evening assembly Swamishri blessed the assembly.

Annakut and Bal Din Today, the women devotees had prepared an annakut of 1151 delicacies to offer to the deities. Swamishri performed the arti and then gave blessings to the devotees, praising the devotion of all and the artistic way in which the annakut was arranged. In the evening assembly, the balaks celebrated the BAPS Children’s Activities Golden Jubilee by presenting a special programme titled ‘Suvarna Bhakti Din’.
After his morning puja Swamishri performed pujan of a large pair of marble charnarvinds (footprints of Bhagwan Swaminarayan) that were to be placed between the two Mayur Dwars in Akshardham complex.

H.H. Chidanandji Maharaj (Muniji), Head, Parmarthniketan, Rishikesh, said, “In the giant Akshardham complex I experienced in every step the darshan of our culture, samskars and the sadhna of sadhus. Here, there is the power of bhakti and seva.”

Shri Rameshbhai Oza, an eloquent propagator of Shrimad Bhagvat, added, “In the 21st century the country which has the richest cultural heritage will be held to be the best. Delhi is the heart of our country and Pramukh Swami Maharaj has established Akshardham in its heart.”

Shri Hridaynarayanji, Scholar in Ancient History, said, “I believe the greatest personal motive in man is to attain moksha. Akshardham has the potential to guide and take one to the doors of this personal motive. For spiritual sadhaks this will forever remain an ideal pillar. In future any sculptor or artist will come here for inspiration. For centuries it will proclaim that Indian culture is not only rich but it is also alive.”

Shri Bhagwat Swaroop, Settlements Commission, Government of India, related, “What has touched me is the dedication of the workers. The complex is a spiritual journey of India’s glorious past. There is a unique blend of India’s glorious past and the present age technology. I would say that I am spiritually enlightened by it and I am sure that whenever anybody visits this monument, he is going to be spiritually inspired by it.”
Living in Vienna, the capital of Austria,

Shri George met Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He has been a dedicated satsangi for years. In 1988, when Swamishri came to Vienna, he too drove Swamishri's car. Recalling that memory today, he said, "When you came, there were two cars before you. You chose me and sat in my car. Today I realise that you sat in my car in order to enter my soul."

ds.t: Why he sat in my car
w: Living in Vienna, the capital city of Austria,

Mr George met Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He has been a devoted satsangi for years. In 1988, when Swamishri visited Vienna, he had driven Swamishri's car. Recalling that today, he said, "When you came, there were two cars in front of you. You chose me and sat in my car. Today I realise that you sat in my car in order to enter my soul."

Today Mahant Swami Maharaj had come to the assembly hall for the welcome assembly, but his entry onto the stage was to be at the time the skit on the "Satpurush" was performed. So he sat on the sofa in the waiting room. Because of this, the volunteers serving there won a lottery of benefit. This unexpected chance of close darshan felt like a dream to them.
Swamishri too got into conversation with these volunteers. Seeing a volunteer named Vijaybhai Nanani, he said, "100 children..."

No one understood the meaning of these words of his. So Vijaybhai himself was asked about it, and he said, "In 1985, when a shibir was held at Nenpur, I was 16 or 17 years old. At that time, in connection with the children's group, I had said to Swamishri, 'Please bless me that my children's assembly has 100 children.'"
Today, 31 years later, Swamishri spoke of this as soon as he saw that volunteer! Hearing this, everyone was lost in wonder at Swamishri's sharp memory.

ds.t: What can I do for unity?
w: In the blessings at today's welcome assembly, giving a lesson on unity, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, "Pramukh Swami Maharaj has left nothing undone. All that remains for us is to put on the garland. We must do what Pramukh Swami Maharaj likes. Yogibapa used to say, 'If there is no friendliness, they will not let you into Akshardham.' Unity is very much needed. All this work has been done through unity. We ourselves must keep unity. If we expect it from the other person, there is trouble. If one thinks, 'Only if the other person keeps it will I keep it', nothing will come of it. There will be conflict and unrest. But if you think, 'What can I do for unity?', unity will remain. Pramukh Swami Maharaj said for unity: 'Tolerate, wear yourself out for others, give up your own will and adjust.' Everything needed for unity is contained in this. (But) we do just what we have decided in our minds, whatever happens to the other person. There is unity among us, but we must keep unity like that in the minds of Yogibapa and Pramukh Swami Maharaj. We may have our natures, but God and the Sant are not going to leave us; if we leave, that is another matter. The more we adjust, the more the benefit."
Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj set off in the car for the airport, Nilkanthjivandas Swami asked, "How is ekantik dharma attained?"
Swamishri answered in one word: "Divyabhav (seeing divinity)."
